;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018 Karachi Chinese consulate attack]]
**Four people are killed in an armed assault on the [[China|Chinese]] consulate in [[Karachi]], [[Pakistan]]. Three attackers are also dead. The attack is claimed by the [[Balochistan Liberation Army]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/11/23/asia/karachi-chinese-consulate-attack-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2018 Orakzai bombing]]
**An explosion kills at least 35 people and injures at least 55 at a market in [[Kalaya]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], northern [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/11/pakistan-deadly-blast-hits-market-orakzai-district-181123072104727.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**At least 26 Afghan security forces are killed and 50 are injured by a suicide blast in a mosque inside an army base in [[Khost Province]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2018-11-23/at-least-26-killed-in-a-blast-in-mosque-in-afghanistan-officials (Reuters via ''U.S. News & World Report'')] 
*Witnesses say that gunmen in pickup trucks attacked a police station in [[Tazirbu]], southeast [[Libya]]. At least five people were killed and several civilians were abducted. [https://www.mytwintiers.com/news/reports-gunmen-kill-at-least-5-in-southeast-libya/1614624665 (AP via WETM TV18)]

;Disasters and accidents
*Four [[Finland|Finnish]] tourists and a Zimbabwean pilot are killed when a [[Cessna 206|Cessna S206]] crashes in [[Masvingo Province]], in southern [[Zimbabwe]]. Two Finnish business leaders were among the dead: {{ill|Pekka Ojanpää|fi}}, the CE of the maintenance services and circular economy company {{ill|Lassila & Tikanoja|fi}}, and {{ill|Heikki Vappula|fi}}, a director of the forestry company [[UPM (company)|UPM]]. [https://yle.fi/uutiset/osasto/news/two_finnish_business_leaders_confirmed_dead_in_zimbabwe_plane_crash/10525112 (Yle)]
*Margaash, an eight year old [[snow leopard]], is shot dead by staff at [[Dudley Zoological Gardens]], [[England]] after escaping its enclosure. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-birmingham-46398647 (BBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[Khadim Hussain Rizvi]], chief of [[Pakistan]]i [[List of political parties in Pakistan|political party]] [[Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan]] (TLP), together with his party leaders, is arrested after TLP's refusal to postpone their call for a public rally planned for 25 November at [[Liaqat National Bagh|Liaqat Bagh]], Rawalpindi. Pakistan's [[Ministry of Information, Broadcasting and National Heritage (Pakistan)|Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting]] [[Fawad Chaudhry]] clarifies that the action has no connection with the [[Asia Bibi blasphemy case|Asia Bibi case]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1447217/ (''Dawn'')], [https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2018/11/23/crackdown-against-tlp-begins-several-arrested/ (''Pakistan Today'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2018 Sri Lankan constitutional crisis]]
**Lawmakers opposed to [[Mahinda Rajapaksa]] as [[Prime Minister of Sri Lanka|Prime Minister]] win a vote for control of a new 13-member [[Parliament of Sri Lanka|parliamentary]] main committee. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sri-lanka-politics/opponents-of-new-sri-lanka-pm-take-control-of-key-committee-idUSKCN1NS0Y3 (Reuters)]
*Workers at [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] distribution centers in Germany and Spain protest labour conditions in a strike coinciding with the [[Black Friday (shopping)|Black Friday]] shopping peak. [https://www.wsfa.com/2018/11/23/amazon-staff-europe-protest-coincide-with-black-friday/ (AP via WSFA)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-amazon-com-strikes-germany/amazon-workers-strike-in-germany-spain-on-black-friday-idUSKCN1NS1AU (Reuters)]
*The [[London]] [[Metropolitan Police Service]] releases video footage of police cars being driven into suspected criminals on scooters. They say the tactic isn't new. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-46321720 (BBC)]

;Sports
*[[Phil Mickelson]] defeats [[Tiger Woods]] after 22 holes of match play at [[Shadow Creek Golf Course]] to win $9 million USD. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/golf/46325735 (BBC)]
